answer: At two unpredictable minutes each epoch, a dune station and a tundra station broadcast a paired signal; each identity returns both halves signed with its own endpoint keys within 400 ms, too short for a relay between sites. So each identity needs a live endpoint at both sites at once. An endpoint can sign for only one identity per window; a second signature from it is public proof zeroing both identities. Auditors verify the signed halves against the schedule, checking keys and timing. Two endpoint slots cost an honest agent $30 an epoch; 1,000 fakes need 2,000 slots, $30,000 an epoch.
